Subjective:
- Presenting complaint: Right knee pain with clicking; reduced running tolerance; occasional tingling in right toes.
- Onset/duration/progression:
  - Symptoms began approximately 2 weeks ago.
  - Pain typically starts ~20 minutes into running (around 2.5–3 miles), sometimes requires stopping; clicking noted with knee flexion/extension during gym exercises; initial mild swelling after first longer run resolved with ice.
  - One episode of tingling in right toes after a run; resolved.
- Past medical history:
  - LASIK (refractive surgery).
  - Prior severe UTI/possible kidney stone requiring ER attendance.
  - Otherwise reports only common minor illnesses.
- Previous injuries/surgeries:
  - Recent fall playing ice hockey several months ago causing a large bruise; no other joint injuries reported.
- Medications:
  - Ibuprofen (takes intermittently; reports up to 400 mg).
  - Aleve (patient-reported; dose/route/frequency not documented; patient uncertain about drug class).
  - Vitamin D (dose/route/frequency not documented).
  - Melatonin (dose/route/frequency not documented).
  - Occasional alprazolam/Xanax (dose/route/frequency not documented).
  - Occasional cannabis use (“smokes a joint”).
- Social history:
  - Active in sports; training for a marathon (recently increased longer runs).
  - Plays ice hockey.
  - Occasional cannabis use.
- Allergies:
  - Not stated.

Objective:
- Functional/movement findings reported by patient:
  - Able to fully straighten and fully flex the affected leg.
  - No locking; no instability described (patient denies episodes of knee “giving way”).
  - No difficulty with stairs or normal walking.
  - Clicking noted with flexion/extension in gym activities and with running.
- Local signs:
  - Mild knee swelling noted after first longer run, resolved with ice; currently not swollen and not painful at rest.
  - Patient reports possible fluid accumulation (self-observation), and some tenderness when pressing (patient-perceived).
- Neurovascular:
  - One transient episode of tingling in right toes after a run; no persistent numbness.
  - No change in color or temperature of lower legs; no calf pain.
- Vitals/exam:
  - No formal vitals or clinician-performed physical exam documented.
- Investigations:
  - None performed or documented.

Assessment & Plan:

1. Right knee pain:
   - Assessment/likely diagnosis: Overuse knee injury
   - Differential diagnosis:
     - Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) injury (patient concern noted)
     - Cartilage/meniscal injury (mentioned by clinician as possibility)
     - Knee effusion/soft tissue injury
   - Investigations planned:
     - Physiotherapy assessment for clinical evaluation
     - Imaging of the knee if indicated based on physiotherapy/clinical findings (type/urgency not specified)
   - Treatment planned:
     - Continue ice therapy as helpful
     - Reduce running intensity/duration; avoid running through pain
     - Stronger anti-inflammatory to be prescribed by clinician (medication name not documented; dose/route/frequency not documented); advised not to take concurrently with ibuprofen and to take with food
   - Relevant referrals:
     - Referral to physiotherapist (to arrange comprehensive assessment and management)
     - Option to be seen in clinic sooner if physiotherapy wait is prolonged

2. Right toe paresthesia (transient):
   - Assessment/likely diagnosis: Transient paresthesia of right toes
   - Differential diagnosis:
     - Not further specified in transcript
   - Investigations planned:
     - None specifically planned; monitor symptoms
   - Treatment planned:
     - No specific treatment documented; advise to report if symptoms persist or recur

3. Patient education / safety-netting:
   - Assessment/likely diagnosis: None (advice only)
   - Differential diagnosis: N/A
   - Investigations planned: N/A
   - Treatment/planned actions:
     - Advised to seek urgent medical review if knee develops persistent swelling, warmth, redness, high temperature, systemic unwellness, or if knee locks and cannot be bent/straightened.
     - Prescription to be sent to pharmacy (stronger anti-inflammatory; details not documented).

Quality checks:
- Missing but expected elements:
  - No clinician-performed physical examination documented (inspection, palpation, ligamentous/meniscal tests).
  - No documented vital signs.
  - Medication names, doses, routes, and frequencies largely not documented (patient-reported medications without dosing details).
  - Allergies not explicitly confirmed.
- Internal conflicts from transcript:
  - Early in the visit patient initially stated “my knees are hurting” then later clarified pain is in the right knee only (conflict noted).
  - Patient uncertain about medication identification (stated “Aleve — think that’s acetaminophen”; classification unclear).
- Transcript quality:
  - Overall adequate and intelligible; some brief conversational overlaps and informal phrasing but clinically relevant information extractable.
